safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(والتين) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم ("I swear") (هذا) is a demonstrative in the position of genitive, conjoined to التين, (البلد) is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative — or an ʿaṭf bayān for it — genitive (اللام) is the lām of oath (قد) is a particle of certainty (في أحسن) is attached to a ḥāl from الإنسان (ثم) is for conjunction (أسفل) is an accusative ḥāl from the third-person pronoun (in رددناه) [Note: or it is an accusative adverbial attached to (رددناه), with an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "a lower place".]..
Clause: « (أقسم) بالتين ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause.
And the clause: «خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the jawāb al-qasam.
And the clause: «رددناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(1) التين: a proper noun for a particular mountain in Syria, or the name of the well-known fruit, a generic noun (ism jins); its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.
(الزيتون): a proper noun for a particular mountain in Syria, or the name of the well-known fruit, a generic noun; its pattern is فعلون, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(2) سينين: a proper noun for a particular mountain in Egypt; it is said that its meaning is "the blessed"; its pattern is فعليل, with kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn.
(4) تقويم: the regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral قوّم; its pattern is تفعيل; its meaning is setting right and straightness.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(إلّا) is for exception [Note: or in the sense of "but" (lākin).], (الذين) is a relative in the position of accusative, an excepted noun, (الفاء) is redundant (لهم) is attached to a fronted khabar for the mubtadaʾ (أجر) , (غير) is a naʿt of أجر, nominative.
Clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «لهم أجر ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive (ما) is an interrogative noun of denial, in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ (بعد) is an adverbial indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative, attached to (يكذّبك) [Note: the adverbial was cut off from annexation in form but not in meaning, so it was made indeclinable on ḍamma; the original sentence is: "What makes you deny after the mention of the creation of man and his return..."], (بالدين) is attached to (يكذّبك).
Clause: «ما يكذّبك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
Shift of person (iltifāt): in His saying, the Exalted «فَما يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِالدِّينِ».
It is an address to man, in the manner of iltifāt from the third person to the second, to intensify the rebuke and silencing, i.e.: what makes you a denier on account of the recompense and your denial of it, after this evidence?

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative of affirmation (أحكم) is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ليس.
Clause: «أليس الله بأحكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(أحكم): the elative from the triliteral حكم, meaning "judged"; its pattern is أفعل.

* Benefits:
- Mention of prepositions that have nothing to attach to:
From our saying "a preposition must have something to attach to" is excepted the redundant preposition, such as the bāʾ and min in His saying, the Exalted (وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً) (هَلْ مِنْ خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ), and that is because the meaning of attachment (taʿalluq) is a semantic connection, and the principle is that verbs fall short of reaching nouns, so they were assisted in that by prepositions. The redundant one enters the sentence only to strengthen and emphasize it, not to connect. And al-Ḥawfī's statement that the bāʾ in His saying, the Exalted (أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ الْحاكِمِينَ) is attached is a mistake. Yes, it is sound to say of the reinforcing lām that it is attached to the reinforced governing element, as in His saying, the Exalted (مُصَدِّقاً لِما مَعَهُمْ) and (فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ) and (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّءْيا تَعْبُرُونَ), because the truth is that it is not purely redundant, given the weakness imagined in the governing element that put it in the position of an intransitive one, nor purely transitivizing, since dropping it is consistently valid; so it has a rank between the two ranks.
